records.heading: 1 Single-stock comparisons
records.text: 1 Single-stock comparisons Each panel overlays one sensitivity model on Base 1.06: all data . LOI and LOO are shown separately below, with the same axes across all eight panels. The solid black line is always the base; the dashed coloured line is the model named in the panel. These are point estimates of spawning biomass for the assessment years, 1970–2026. The model reports biomass in thousand tonnes; values below are divided by 1,000 to show million tonnes. Only the recent index groups are varied: Chile CPUE, Offshore CPUE, both Peru CPUEs, and Chile Acoustic N. As implemented in run_loo.R , “left out” means that the index error is multiplied by 100, strongly reducing its weight. Other indices, catches and composition data retain their base treatment.

records.title: Assessment index sensitivities: LOI and LOO
records.heading: 1.1 LOI — leave one in
records.text: 1.1 LOI — leave one in The named recent index group retains its base weight; the other recent groups are downweighted. The LOI runs showed substantial differences in the scale of recent spawning biomass. Retaining North Chile acoustics (Chile Acoustic N; model 3.04) produced the highest 2026 estimate, 24.28 million tonnes, compared with 6.11 million tonnes in the all-data base (297% higher). Retaining both Peru CPUE series (3.03) also produced a much higher estimate, 13.22 million tonnes (116% higher). The Offshore CPUE-only run (3.02) was closer to the base at 7.10 million tonnes (16% higher), whereas the Chile CPUE-only run (3.01) was lower at 4.61 million tonnes (25% lower). These results indicate contrasting signals among the recent index groups, with particularly strong recovery in the North Chile acoustic-only run. records.title: Assessment index sensitivities: LOI and LOO
records.heading: 1.2 LOO — leave one out
records.text: 1.2 LOO — leave one out The named recent index group is downweighted; the other groups retain their base weights. The largest LOO response occurred when Chile CPUE was left out (model 3.05): estimated 2026 spawning biomass increased to 11.80 million tonnes, 93% above the base. Leaving out North Chile acoustics (3.08) had the opposite effect, reducing the estimate to 4.31 million tonnes (30% below the base) and producing a declining trajectory in the most recent years. Leaving out Offshore CPUE (3.06) or both Peru CPUE series (3.07) had smaller effects, with 2026 estimates of 6.60 and 6.73 million tonnes, respectively (8% and 10% above the base). Taken together, the two analyses show that North Chile acoustics support higher recent biomass, while Chile CPUE restrains it within the fitted model. The high biomass in the Peru CPUE-only run does not translate into a large decrease when those indices are left out; their omission instead produces a modest increase. The effects therefore depend on which other indices remain in the model, and cannot be summarized as a uniformly positive or negative influence of every index across both analyses. records.heading: What do catches and surveys tell us?
records.text: What do catches and surveys tell us? Are changes in the observations telling us that fish abundance has changed, or that the fish are being encountered differently? An abundance index is a series used to track changes in the quantity of fish. Interpreting one requires understanding where, when and how the observations were collected.

records.title: Catches and surveys
records.heading: What the papers show
records.text: What the papers show The submitted papers examine catches, fishery catch rates, acoustic surveys and biological sampling. Some abundance signals differ. One paper reports an increasing standardised index in 2026, while another describes a marked early-year decline. These author-reported results call for a comparison on a consistent basis before drawing stock-status conclusions. Sources: JM10 , JM15 .

records.title: Catches and surveys
records.heading: Why it matters for management
records.text: Why it matters for management A catch rate can change because abundance changes, but also because fishing location, fleet behaviour, technology or fish availability changes. Acoustic surveys provide another view, with their own coverage and interpretation issues. Reliable advice depends on understanding these differences before choosing the information used in the assessment.

How can we choose rules that support catches while performing acceptably when the future is uncertain? Management strategy evaluation ( MSE ) tests management procedures in simulated fisheries. A procedure specifies how information is used to make a decision, such as a catch recommendation. The simulation repeats the process over time so that the consequences of earlier decisions affect later ones.

records.title: Jack mackerel base model: MCMC uncertainty
records.heading: What uncertainty is covered?
records.text: What uncertainty is covered? MCMC explores parameter uncertainty conditional on this single-stock model. Alternative stock hypotheses, additional processes, different data treatments and fixed parameter choices can be assessed through separate sensitivity analyses. The defaults initialize every chain at the same mode. A run that needs further work should be followed by a separately labelled analysis with justified changes to initialization, run length or sampler controls. The Kobe calculation constructs stock-wide fishing mortality from F at age across all four fleets. The model’s native Fbar field describes a fishery-specific parameter, and its depletion fields describe total-biomass ratios. The source notes record these definitions so each reported quantity retains its biological meaning.

records.text: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide Proposed advice and decisions for discussion before Commission consideration Published September 10, 2026 Results working paper · Retained-CMP scorecard · All-CMP scorecard · Jack mackerel wiki Note Draft for discussion This guide proposes a route from the current scientific comparison to a Commission decision. The shortlist, responsibilities and wording are proposed for review by the Scientific Committee, Commission and Parties. They draw on the saved 500-simulation results in the companion working paper. Selection of a management procedure remains a decision for the Commission.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 1 Proposed advice for the next discussion
records.text: 1 Proposed advice for the next discussion Candidate management procedures (CMPs) are rules for turning monitoring information into catch advice. Operating models (OMs) represent possible stock and fishery conditions; robustness tests check the rules under alternative assumptions. Carry HS−20 (MP43), HS−30 (MP47) and PR−20 (MP44) forward as a small set for focused scientist–manager discussion. They preserve the contrast between catch stability, the ability to make larger advice reductions, and the power-ramp response. Use the fixed-catch run as a reference comparison. Keep the full CMP set available so that an omitted alternative can be reinstated if agreed objectives or robustness tests justify it. The immediate recommendation is to agree the criteria for selecting among these alternatives. Choosing a preferred CMP depends on managers’ priorities. A score of 100 marks the best selected value for an indicator. Biological acceptability also requires an agreed risk limit.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 1.1 Suggested wording for consideration
records.text: 1.1 Suggested wording for consideration The Scientific Committee is invited to consider carrying HS−20, HS−30 and PR−20 forward for focused consultation, subject to review of the screening criteria and remaining projection checks. The comparison should present reference-OM performance and separate recruitment-crash (OM11_2) and recruitment-cycle (OM11_3) robustness results, with near-term 2026–2035 trade-off and Kobe plots. Managers are invited to specify the biological performance requirements and the relative importance of catch, catch variability and the ability to reduce advice. A subsequent recommendation for a preferred CMP should state these choices, identify the supporting results and specify implementation, responses to unexpected conditions and review arrangements. This wording proposes a process and a set of CMPs for discussion. Confirming that these CMPs meet biological requirements will require an agreed standard and a check of their performance against it. The advice-reduction update changes the earlier screening result: HS+20, HSsym, PR+20 and PRsym now show trade-offs with the listed comparators. The three-CMP display remains a discussion set, and all eight CMPs should be reviewed before confirming the shortlist.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 2 Why retain these alternatives?
records.text: 2 Why retain these alternatives? IACC measures annual catch variability. SSB is spawning-stock biomass, and Blim is the biomass limit. “Green” means biomass and fishing pressure meet the stated MSY reference levels; the definitions below explain the time period and changing biomass reference. Alternative Management choice it helps examine Results and points to consider HS−20 (MP43) Greater emphasis on stable catches, retaining the 20% advice-reduction limit. Lower reference IACC than PR−20; compare the biological consequences as well as stability in the reference trade-offs . HS−30 (MP47) Whether allowing larger advice reductions provides a worthwhile biological benefit. Lower reference below-previous-Blim frequency than HS−20, with a different frequency of advice reductions greater than 19%. Review both outcomes in the reference comparison . PR−20 (MP44) Whether higher reference catch and its biological performance justify greater catch variability. Highest long-term dynamic-green probability among these three in recruitment crash (54.5%) and recruitment cycle (51.5%). See the focused robustness results . Fixed catch What is gained or lost by responding to observations rather than holding advice constant. A reference comparison; evaluation under the alternative OMs would be needed before considering it alongside the finalists. Its saved recruitment deviations, implementation adjustments and MSY values differ from the other reference runs; see the comparison limits . For this stage, retaining contrasting alternatives is more defensible than selecting the top three from one composite ranking. This approach keeps the main choices visible while leaving room to revisit alternatives with useful advantages. If managers prefer numerical ranking, first agree the indicators, weights and biological requirements, then check whether the preferred CMP changes with those choices and with OM selection. The scorecards support this exploration. A systematic check of how rankings change with the selected weights and OMs remains to be completed.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 3 Decisions and actions to record
records.text: 3 Decisions and actions to record The following division of responsibilities is proposed for discussion. The final process and the Party or Parties tabling a Commission proposal remain to be agreed. Decision What needs to be recorded Results or next action 1. Biological objectives Target status, limit definition, acceptable risk, assessment period, and whether requirements apply to each stock component or to an aggregate. Scientists should express each requirement as a reproducible statistic; managers should confirm the required performance. Keep the current 60% dynamic-green tuning convention distinct from any newly requested target. 2. Role of robustness tests Which scenarios determine acceptability, which inform contingency planning, and any agreed OM weights. Review recruitment crash (OM11_2) and recruitment cycle (OM11_3) separately. Compare the near-term 2026–2035 displays with long-term outcomes; agree a method before combining results across OMs. 3. Shortlist and preferences Whether to retain these three CMPs; which differences matter; whether any composite weights are agreed. Review the full-set scorecard and screening tolerances. Retain or reinstate an alternative if it offers a relevant advantage under the agreed criteria. 4. Stability and response Allowed increases and decreases in advice, management-cycle length, implementation lag and any phase-in provisions. Distinguish advice limits from realized-catch variability. Evaluate any changed settings before recommending the revised package. 5. Preferred CMP Exact CMP identifier, tuning and settings; reasons for choosing it; material disadvantages accepted. Scientists should document performance against agreed criteria. A Party proposal could then identify the preferred package for Commission consideration. Delegations would state their preferences during that process. 6. Implementation and review Required data and deadlines, responsibility for running and checking the MP, first application, missing-data procedures, response to unexpected conditions, and scheduled review. Prepare an implementation plan alongside the proposal. Agree when a review is required, who will conduct it, and a timetable suited to SPRFMO.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 4 Definitions that must accompany the advice
records.text: 4 Definitions that must accompany the advice Tuning and risk answer different questions. Here, dynamic-green results concern SSB at or above dynamic BMSY and F at or below FMSY over the stated 2041–2050 period. The probability of staying above a biomass limit throughout the period requires a separate calculation. The figures labelled SSB/SSBMSY describe biomass relative to the stored, fixed reference value; dynamic-green probabilities use a reference value that changes with productivity. Count years below a limit and simulations with a breach separately. The existing SSB <8% dynamic B0 statistic is the fraction of simulation-years below the previous Blim. If managers instead require the probability of at least one breach during a specified period, that statistic must be calculated separately. The 8% threshold represents the previous Blim for this comparison. Managers still need to confirm the limit and acceptable risk for adoption. Advice reductions cover all annual comparisons. CatchDrop20 now reports the percentage of valid comparisons in which HCR advice falls strictly more than 19%, pooled across all years and 500 iterations. Exact 20% reductions count, and no biomass filter is applied. This measures advice before implementation; realized-catch variability remains available separately. The first advice is compared with the saved HCR initial advice, or the constant target for fixed catch, giving 25 years × 500 iterations = 12,500 comparisons. See the working paper for denominators and the two-stock advice convention.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 5 Work needed before recommending adoption
records.text: 5 Work needed before recommending adoption Confirm the biological requirements and how robustness outcomes affect selection. If these differ from the evaluated settings, rerun or retune the affected comparisons. Complete the remaining projection checks and document the results, including low-catch failures and advice-versus-realized-catch discrepancies. The revised advice statistic does not resolve underlying projection problems. Review the new 2026–2035 trade-off and Kobe plots alongside long-term summaries. A separate first-application reduction distribution would further inform implementation. If fixed catch is proposed as an adoption candidate, evaluate it under comparable recruitment and implementation assumptions and the required robustness set. Its present role is a reference comparison. Hold a focused scientist–manager and stakeholder discussion, record preferences and remaining disagreements, and prepare a preferred-CMP proposal with a complete implementation and review specification.

records.title: Jack mackerel management procedure: draft decision guide
records.heading: 6 How the supplied examples inform this guide
records.text: 6 How the supplied examples inform this guide The ICCAT Atlantic bluefin decision guide (2022) , especially pages 3–4, 7 and 24, separates safety, stock status, management cycle, stability, MP choice and review. It links these choices to performance tables and an interactive results application. Its safety statistic concerns the lowest depletion within each simulation over a defined period; that is different from our frequency of years below a limit. This guide follows that sequence of decisions. SPRFMO would agree its own thresholds, scoring method and review interval. The IOTC bigeye MP adoption document (2022) , especially printed pages 1 and 3–5, compares two remaining CMPs by their practical advantages, then asks the Commission to choose a tuning objective and an MP. It refers implementation and exceptional-circumstances arrangements to supporting documents. This supports keeping the main decision guide short while linking the detailed results and specifying the remaining actions. Review of the supplied ICES download link awaits access to the file, and review of the draft supplement awaits a copy. The proposals above draw on the two documents reviewed. Their application to jack mackerel was developed for this guide.

records.heading: 2 Data, periods and indicator definitions
records.text: 2 Data, periods and indicator definitions The results cover eight candidate management procedures (CMPs), each with 500 simulations under the reference operating model (OM) and nine alternative OMs used to test performance under different assumptions (robustness tests). Two-stock OMs are shown by biological component; their catches and biomasses are reported separately. Advice reductions use all annual advice comparisons across all iterations (advice years 2025–2049 , applied 2026–2050 ). The near-term plots and biological probabilities use 2026–2035 . Long-term performance calculations use 2041–2050 , except the inherited mean-catch-reduction column available as an optional scorecard indicator, which uses 2026–2050 . The worm plots span 2025–2050 . For catch, interannual catch change (IACC), and SSB/SSBMSY, first calculate each simulation’s mean over 2041–2050. Trade-off points then show the median across 500 simulations; horizontal and vertical bars show the 25th–75th percentiles. The bars contain the middle half of simulation-specific values. Uncertainty in the estimated median would require a separate calculation. IACC is the absolute percentage change from the previous year’s realized catch. The 2041 change therefore uses catch in 2040. The biomass ratio in the trade-off plots uses the stored static SSBMSY denominator; it is distinct from the dynamic-B0 risk indicator. The low-biomass indicator is the proportion of simulation-years with SSB <8% of the matching year’s dynamic B0 , the previous Blim. Dynamic B0 is the saved projected unfished SSB for the matching simulation. Each year below the threshold counts, including consecutive years. Catch below 270 kt is also a pooled simulation-year frequency. The advice-reduction frequency ( CatchDrop20 ) is the proportion of valid annual HCR-advice comparisons with \(A_t < 0.81 A_{t-1}\) , pooled over all years and 500 iterations. Advice is recorded in 2025–2049 and applied in 2026–2050. The first advice is compared with the saved HCR initial advice, or the constant advice target for fixed catch. This gives 25 comparisons per iteration (12,500 when complete). Exact 19% reductions and increases do not count; 20% reductions count. There are no biomass or near-20% exclusions. Invalid values and nonpositive previous advice are excluded from the denominator and reported in the audit. This uses advice before implementation. Two-stock OMs have advice for the managed Southern stock; the same run-level advice statistic appears in both component views. records.text: 4 Scorecards: best 100, others relative to it Use the all-CMP scorecard to review the original set and the retained-set scorecard for the retained-set comparison and fixed-catch reference comparison. Both open with best-relative scaling and equal weights on the available screening indicators. Use Choose an OM to select reference (OM11), recruitment crash (OM11_2), or recruitment cycle (OM11_3) . Scores are recomputed separately within each OM. The full nine-OM robustness plots and data remain available in the expandable appendix below. The fixed-catch benchmark is available in the reference selection only. The supplied fixed-catch results cover the reference OM. When fixed catch is selected, the two vulnerable-biomass indicators are unavailable pending extraction from the supplied run; deselect it to restore those choices. Each scorecard displays only indicators shared by the selected CMPs. The fixed-catch snapshot uses its own stored reference points and reconstructed dynamic B0, preserving its reported tuning convention. Users can change CMPs, indicators, scaling and weights. The overall score helps explore preferences. The revised five-indicator comparison requires the earlier shortlist to be reviewed. For a higher-is-better indicator, the score is \(100V_i/\max_j(V_j)\) . For a lower-is-better indicator, it is \(100\min_j(V_j)/V_i\) . The best value therefore scores 100. Scores are recalculated for the selected CMP set, so each selection has its own reference for comparison. Zero-best exception: when the best value for a lower-is-better indicator is zero, zero-valued CMPs score 100 and positive-valued CMPs score zero. This rule is necessary because the ordinary ratio cannot distinguish positive values when its numerator is zero. In the full reference set, several CMPs and fixed catch have zero advice reductions greater than 19%, while HS−20, HS−30, PR−20 and PR−30 have positive frequencies. This gives the latter zero scores for this indicator when a zero-valued comparator is selected. Inspect the raw frequencies and compare with range scaling before assigning weight. Related stock or stability indicators can overlap even when given equal weights. The existing general best-relative explorer and original range-scaled explorer provide the broader application context. records.heading: 10 Decisions this paper can support
records.text: 10 Decisions this paper can support The companion draft decision guide uses these results to propose advice, a manager decision checklist and the work needed before an adoption recommendation. It is a discussion draft for review by the Scientific Committee, managers and Parties. Review the explicit screening tolerances and decide whether the three-CMP presentation set is sufficient for the next discussion. Set biological acceptability criteria separately from best-relative scoring; a relatively high score can coexist with unacceptable risk. Examine robustness panels and the full-set data before treating an omitted CMP as dispensable. Agree which indicators and weights represent the objectives, paying particular attention to zero-best risk indicators and overlapping measures. Retain projection-failure diagnostics and advice-versus-realized-catch checks as outstanding validation work. The advice statistic measures decisions before implementation; failed projections and their effects on realized-catch indicators still require investigation.

records.text: Footnotes For each PI \(x\) , the best-performing CMP among the \(N\) selected CMPs is assigned a weight of 100. For a PI where higher values are preferred, CMP \(i\) receives \(W_{i,x}=100\,V_{i,x}/V_{\mathrm{best},x}\) , where \(V_{\mathrm{best},x}=\max_j(V_{j,x})\) . For a PI where lower values are preferred, the calculation is: \(W_{i,x}=100\,V_{\mathrm{best},x}/V_{i,x}\) , where \(V_{\mathrm{best},x}=\min_j(V_{j,x})\) . Thus the best CMP has \(W_{i,x}=100\) , while the other weights retain their proportional contrast with the best observed value. records.title: Second CMP screening comparison: MP29, MP45 and MP43
records.heading: 1 Findings for discussion
records.text: 1 Findings for discussion The three hockey-stick CMPs have similar reference median catch and IACC, but differ in low-catch risk, biomass risk and the probability of advice reductions greater than 19%. MP29 and MP45 have zero occurrences of those advice reductions in the reference runs; MP43 has 761 occurrences in 12,500 comparisons (6.09%). MP45 has the lowest median IACC of these three, and MP43 has the highest median catch. Those catch and IACC differences are small relative to the inherited screening tolerances. Under the same five-indicator tolerances as the first paper, MP29 compares favourably with both alternatives, and MP45 compares favourably with MP43. These are tolerance-based comparisons, not strict dominance: small disadvantages in other indicators remain visible in the table. All three remain in this comparison. Robustness performance and agreed biological requirements remain separate considerations.

records.heading: 2 Data, periods and indicator definitions
records.text: 2 Data, periods and indicator definitions The source results cover eight candidate management procedures (CMPs), each with 500 simulations; this document focuses on three. The same runs were evaluated under the reference operating model (OM) and nine alternative OMs used to test performance under different assumptions (robustness tests). Two-stock OMs are shown by biological component; their catches and biomasses are reported separately. Advice reductions use all annual advice comparisons across all iterations (advice years 2025–2049 , applied 2026–2050 ). The near-term plots and biological probabilities use 2026–2035 . Long-term performance calculations use 2041–2050 , except the inherited mean-catch-reduction column available as an optional scorecard indicator, which uses 2026–2050 . The worm plots span 2025–2050 . For catch, interannual catch change (IACC), and SSB/SSBMSY, first calculate each simulation’s mean over 2041–2050. Trade-off points then show the median across 500 simulations; horizontal and vertical bars show the 25th–75th percentiles. The bars contain the middle half of simulation-specific values. Uncertainty in the estimated median would require a separate calculation. IACC is the absolute percentage change from the previous year’s realized catch. The 2041 change therefore uses catch in 2040. The biomass ratio in the trade-off plots uses the stored static SSBMSY denominator; it is distinct from the dynamic-B0 risk indicator. The low-biomass indicator is the proportion of simulation-years with SSB <8% of the matching year’s dynamic B0 , the previous Blim. Dynamic B0 is the saved projected unfished SSB for the matching simulation. Each year below the threshold counts, including consecutive years. Catch below 270 kt is also a pooled simulation-year frequency. The probability of an advice reduction ( CatchDrop20 ) is the proportion of valid annual HCR-advice comparisons with \(A_t < 0.81 A_{t-1}\) , pooled over all years and 500 iterations. Advice is recorded in 2025–2049 and applied in 2026–2050. The first advice is compared with the saved HCR initial advice, or the constant advice target for fixed catch. This gives 25 comparisons per iteration (12,500 when complete). Exact 19% reductions and increases do not count; 20% reductions count. There are no biomass or near-20% exclusions. Invalid values and nonpositive previous advice are excluded from the denominator and reported in the audit. This uses advice before implementation. Two-stock OMs have advice for the managed Southern stock; the same run-level advice statistic appears in both component views. For a higher-is-better indicator, the score is \(100V_i/\max_j(V_j)\) . For a lower-is-better indicator, it is \(100\min_j(V_j)/V_i\) . The best value therefore scores 100. records.heading: One stock or more?
records.text: One stock or more? Could a combined view of jack mackerel hide differences between parts of the population? The answer affects how catches and regional observations are interpreted, and whether a management rule performs acceptably for all the population components represented in the analysis.

records.title: One stock or more?
records.heading: What the research has examined
records.text: What the research has examined The benchmark and management evaluation consider alternatives that represent jack mackerel as one stock or as two stocks. They examine how those assumptions affect the analysis. These alternatives test the consequences of different biological explanations; assessing their plausibility requires empirical evidence. Sources: JM02 , JM03 , JM06 , JM07 .

records.title: One stock or more?
records.heading: Why it matters for management
records.text: Why it matters for management A favourable result for the population as a whole may conceal a less favourable result in one component. Where an evaluation represents more than one component, its results should be examined for each as well as in total. The questions raised for SC14 include this concern. Source: JM06 .

records.text: What remains uncertain? Bringing together the earlier genetic, tagging, distribution and modelling studies is the next historical research priority. Managers should be able to see what evidence supports each explanation, and how much the advice changes between them. Questions for a closer scientific review Which stock representation is used in the assessment, and which alternatives are tested in the management evaluation? How are movement, regional catches and abundance indices represented? Are performance measures reported for each population component?

records.title: TAC calculations: 2027–2028
records.heading: How the index is calculated
records.text: How the index is calculated The five series are Chile Acoustic North, Chile CPUE, Peru artisanal CPUE, Peru industrial CPUE and offshore CPUE. Each series is scaled to its own mean over 2019–2023 . The calculation gives equal weight to the available standardized indices within each year, followed by equal weight to the three annual combined indices. Reference mean for each series: reference mean = mean(available observations in 2019–2023) . Standardized index: standardized value = observation / that series’ reference mean . Annual combined index: annual index = mean(available standardized values in that year) . Advice indicator: I = mean(the three annual combined indices ending at the data cutoff) . This sequence follows the estimator saved with the SC14 release. The indicator is dimensionless. It uses equal weighting of available indices; assessment CV adjustments do not change those weights. Year Available indices Annual combined index 2023 5 1.1790266300 2024 5 1.0040530352 2025 5 1.0864224544 2026 4 0.7694876534 For 2027 advice , I = (2023 annual index + 2024 annual index + 2025 annual index) / 3 = 1.0898340398 . For 2028 advice , I = (2024 annual index + 2025 annual index + 2026 annual index) / 3 = 0.9533210476 . Data qualification: Chile Acoustic North has no 2022 observation, so its reference mean uses four observations. Offshore CPUE ends in 2025, so the 2026 annual combination uses the other four series. Missing observations are omitted at the corresponding averaging step, and no offshore value is imputed. The through-2026 calculation is conditional on the currently available 2026 observations, including current-year CPUE values. Both cutoffs use the same current historical data vintage, with observations after each cutoff excluded. This describes a cutoff comparison using the current Model 1.06 data; earlier meeting-year data vintages may differ.

records.title: TAC calculations: 2027–2028
records.heading: How the TAC is calculated
records.text: How the TAC is calculated Let I be the three-year indicator, trigger be the CMP-specific threshold, and previous TAC be the value against which annual changes are constrained. All eight CMPs use an index limit of 0.1 and a minimum raw advice value of 270 kt . For the hockey-stick rules (HS: CMP29, CMP43, CMP45 and CMP47): If I <= 0.1: raw TAC = 270 If 0.1 < I < trigger: raw TAC = 270 + (I - 0.1) * (2000 - 270) / (trigger - 0.1) If I >= trigger: raw TAC = 2000 For the power-ramp rules (PR: CMP32, CMP44, CMP46 and CMP48), first calculate x = (I - 0.1) / (trigger - 0.1) : If I <= 0.1: raw TAC = 270 If 0.1 < I < trigger: raw TAC = 270 + (1500 - 270) * x^2.5 If I >= trigger: raw TAC = 1500 * (0.2 + 0.8 * x)^0.6 The power-ramp upper branch continues to increase above the trigger. Both indicators in this calculation are between 0.1 and every CMP trigger, so the middle branch is used for all eight candidates. The same final step applies to every CMP: Lower limit = previous TAC * lower annual multiplier Upper limit = previous TAC * upper annual multiplier TAC advice = MAX(lower limit, MIN(upper limit, raw TAC)) For 2027, the previous TAC is the scenario value of 1,675 or 1,092 kt in 2026 . For 2028, it is the calculated 2027 advice for the same CMP and starting scenario, retained at full precision. These scenario values replace the 1,385 kt initialization used in the simulation setup. The advice is a total TAC before allocation among fisheries or areas.

records.heading: Sources and reproducibility
records.text: Sources and reproducibility The definitions come from the SC14-MSE-2026-RC1 common 500-draw release , using its CMP registry, candidate controls and tuning summary. The saved estimator and harvest-control functions define the calculation. The release uses identifiers MP29 , MP45 , and so on; this page uses the equivalent CMP29 , CMP45 labels. The input observations come from the current Model 1.06 assessment input , selected by the SC14 assessment configuration. The calculation uses Chile CPUE from SC14-JM10, Peru industrial and artisanal updates supplied for the assessment, offshore CPUE through 2025 from SC14-JM21, and Chile Acoustic North updated through 2026. Read the assessment and find the source papers . The workbook and CSV files retain full precision; the tables here display TACs to two decimals. The downloads make the raw advice, previous TAC, annual bounds, final advice and binding rule available for each calculation. All 32 CMP/year/scenario calculations were compared with direct calls to the saved SC14 functions. The explicit formulas agree within 0.000000000001 kt . Additional checks cover the lower, middle and upper branches of all eight rules. The Excel formulas were also recalculated independently, with all 32 advice results reproduced. These checks establish numerical agreement with the saved candidate definitions; adoption and annual application arrangements are matters for the relevant decision record.
